title: Deviation signatures & telemetry playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working PRD for capturing and surfacing 'deviation signatures' (compact cryptographic markers plus contextual telemetry) emitted when customer-managed network or operator actions deviate from an expected change plan. The playbook ties audit evidence to approval gates so that operators, customers, and internal review processes can reason about what actually happened, quickly triage, and — where necessary — roll back safely.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Event model and minimal evidence payload for a deviation snapshot (what we persist to the immutable evidence store)
- Signature strategy (how to bind a change to approval decisions and runtime telemetry)
- Integration points with approval gates and the operator UI/CLI
- Retention and export rules for customer-managed networking flows (VPC, peering, on-prem connectors)
- Runbook sketches for detection -> attest -> rollback workflows

Non-goals (out of scope):
- Full legal/compliance language for evidence admissibility (legal will take this forward after technical design)
- Deep storage optimizer (we'll iterate after initial telemetry volume analysis)

Background / problem statement:
Customers in private deployments want:
- A compact, tamper-evident record that ties (a) the approval decision, (b) the operator action, and (c) runtime telemetry at the moment of change.
- Quick index/search for suspicious deviations (e.g., allowed change executed with unexpected egress or different CIDR scope).
- A clear rollback trigger that can be automated or manually executed with sufficient evidence to satisfy auditors.

Current status: fragmented logs across control plane agents, operator CLI, and customer-side connectors; approval decisions live in a separate service. We need a single minimal evidence packet emitted at the critical handoff points and a simple signature scheme to bind them.

Goals / success criteria:
- Evidence packet must be <= 3KB (target) for typical change snapshot to reduce storage blowup in high-frequency environments.
- Ability to reconstruct a chain: approval id -> operator identity -> short runtime snapshot (network routes affected, active connections summary) -> compact signature hash.
- Integrate with existing approval gates APIs so every approved change can surface its evidence link in the approval UI and in postmortems.
- Acceptance tests: simulated change with mismatch (approved expected CIDR X, actual applied CIDR Y) should show deviation alert in console within 30s and provide a single-click rollback suggestion.

Design overview (high level):
1) When an approval is recorded, approval service issues an ApprovalToken (UUID) and stores the decision record (who, why, TTL). ApprovalToken is short-lived (configurable).
2) Operator agent (on customer side or operator-run bridge) performs the change; at commit time it emits a DeviationEvidence packet to the evidence-ingest endpoint and includes: approval_token, operator_id, delta_summary, telemetry_digest, wall_time, and operator_signature.
3) evidence-ingest persists packet to an append-only store and calculates an evidence_id (sha256 of canonicalized packet). That evidence_id is returned and appended to the original approval record (cross-link).
4) Rules engine compares delta_summary against approval expectations (policy) and can mark evidence with status: expected | marginal | deviation.

Minimal DeviationEvidence packet (textual example, canonicalized ordering):
- approval_token: PD-xxxx-uuid
- operator_id: email or service principal
- op_action: apply-change|rollback|patch
- target_scope: CIDR(s)/resource ids (short list)
- delta_summary: textual short digest of what was changed (50-200 chars)
- telemetry_digest: base64(HMAC-SHA256 of concatenated small telemetry blob)
- wall_time: 2025-11-03T14:42:13Z
- agent_version: 0.8.1
- operator_signature: base64(sig over canonical packet using operator key)

Notes: keep the telemetry blob small: e.g., top-5 route changes, top-3 active connections hash, sample latency bucket. Telemetry itself is stored separately (and can be sampled), but the digest binds that telemetry to the packet.

Signature strategy options (tradeoffs):
A) Operator key (recommended initial): operator agent holds an RSA/ECDSA keypair (or HSM-backed key for enterprise). Agent signs the canonical evidence packet prior to sending. Pros: simple to verify; clearly attributable. Cons: key management on customer side for private deployments (we provide policy + agent helpers).
B) Approval-service co-sign (m-of-2): approval service can also sign after ingest, producing a combined signature. Pros: stronger non-repudiation, ties approval to action. Cons: more complex flow and latency.

We recommend starting with (A) and iterating towards (B) for customers with stronger audit needs.

Approval gate integration:
- UI: approval record shows evidence_id link and small summary with status. If status==deviation, show top-3 reasons and a recommended rollback action.
- API: GET /approvals/{id}/evidence -> list of evidence_ids and verdicts. POST /evidence/{id}/flag -> add reviewer annotation, trigger retention hold.
- Policy engine hooks: policies can mark certain deviations as auto-rollback. Default: no auto-rollback for network-massive-changes, but enable for small-scoped mistakes (typo CIDR).

Retention and export:
- Evidence packets (small) retained by default 2 years for enterprise customers, 90 days for standard. Telemetry referenced by evidence_digest is stored sampled: high-fidelity for 30 days, aggregated snapshots for 2 years.
- Export formats: evidence bundle (zip) with evidence.json + signed telemetry snapshot + raw logs (if permitted). Support S3/GS export and on-demand download from console.

Runbook sketch (detect -> review -> remediate):
- Detect: rules engine flags evidence as deviation. Immediately generate an incident with priority derived from affected resources (control-plane, customer-facing, egress). Notify on-call via PagerDuty + Slack channel.
- Triage: automated triage attaches diff view (approved vs applied), operator identity, and quick links to netflow sample. Owner reviews and marks as false-positive or confirmed.
- Remediate: if confirmed and policy allows, present single-click rollback (uses stored pre-change snapshot or preflight). If manual rollback chosen, populate CLI command and audit the action as a new evidence packet.

Interoperability with customer-managed pieces:
- For air-gapped or heavily restricted customers, operator agent can sign evidence and instead of sending to our cloud store, produce a signed bundle that customer uploads to a customer-controlled storage endpoint we index (pull model). Work with security team for S3 presigned flows.

Open questions / risks / TODOs (collaborative list):
- Key bootstrapping UX: how does an operator agent get an initial key? (suggestion: preflight generate and have customer upload public key during onboarding).
- Evidence packet size vs fidelity: iterative telemetry sampling experiments needed. TODO: run synthetic workload to estimate 95th percentile packet rate and disk needs.
- Legal: need sign-off on signature scheme acceptance for auditors in EU/UK. Put on legal review.
- Rollback safety: how to guarantee that rollback command won't itself create new deviations? Need a simulated dry-run flag and safety checks.

MVP rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): implement canonical packet + operator signature path in agent; basic evidence-ingest API; append-only persistence; link to approval record. Smoke test in staging.
- Phase 1 (6 weeks): rules engine verdicts, UI integration (evidence link and verdict badge), simple rollback suggestion flow for low-risk changes.
- Phase 2 (8 weeks): sampling telemetry store, export bundles, enterprise key management options, co-sign prototype.

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Test A: approval expected CIDR 10.1.0.0/24, operator applied 10.1.0.0/16 -> evidence shows deviation, verdict=deviation, rollback suggestion present, evidence_id cross-linked.
- Test B: operator agent in air-gapped site produces signed bundle; upload to presigned S3; evidence-ingest verifies signature and indexes it.

Notes for implementers (practical):
- Use canonical JSON ordering for packet hashing. Document canonicalization rules in a separate short spec.
- Keep telemetry blob fields stable (schema v1) and include agent_version in every packet.
- Prefer HMAC-SHA256 for telemetry_digest; prefer ed25519 for operator signatures if possible (compact, fast).

Questions for reviewers:
- Priya: can product commit to the 3KB target? If not, what is acceptable initial size?
- SRE: how many evidence packets per minute can our append-only store handle under Dedicated workloads?
- Legal: flag for evidence admissibility in EU breaches.

Appendix (quick checklist):
- [ ] canonicalization spec (write)
- [ ] agent key bootstrap UX (design)
- [ ] retention policy proposal for enterprise vs standard (finalize)
- [ ] CI acceptance test harness (simulate mismatched changes)

---
Notes-to-self: this is intentionally lightweight; don't try to encode full netflow in the evidence packet. Keep packet as the binding glue and use sampling/exports for deep forensic work.
